answer: Each epoch, every agent's work is graded by a panel drawn by verifiable randomness, revealed only when scoring starts. An attacker cannot know who judges any identity, so bribing a fixed jury never pays. To sway a verdict they must corrupt a large sample of staked agents, and each failed bribe burns their stake and slashes the judge's reputation. A fake identity must bond stake and survive many panels before its votes count, so flooding the dawn market, drifting through the ocean of agents, or hiding on the tundra costs more than honest work.
